question: A man travels from point A to B at a speed of 56(1)/(4) km/h and returns to A through same route by increasing his speed by 33(1)/(3)\% of his earlier speed. His average speed (in km/h) for the whole journey is
solution:
**Given:**

A man goes from place A to B at a speed of 56(1)/(4) km/h and returns by increasing his speed by 33(1)/(3)\% of his earlier speed.

Speed1 = 56(1)/(4)km/h = 225/4 km/h

Speed2 = Speed1 + 33(1)/(3)\% of speed1 

= (225)/(4) km/h + 33(1)/(3)\% × (225)/(4) km/h

= (225)/(4) + (225)/(12) = (900)/(12) =75 km/h

**Formula used:**

Average speed = 2× speed ₁ × speed₂over speed₁+ speed₂ (**This formula is only applicable when the distance is the same )**

**Calculation:**

Average speed = 2× speed ₁ × speed₂over speed₁+ speed₂

= ​2× {225over 4} × 75 over {225over4 }+75

= {450 over 7}

Average speed = 64{2 over 7} km/h

Hence, the average speed (in km/h) for the whole journey is 64{2 over 7} km/h.​​​
